_: Every number the extractor tunes with, in one file, because none of them is a fact about a canvas. They are all expressed at a fixed working resolution -- px_per_cm below -- so a brush stroke is the same physical object on every canvas and a smoothing scale transfers unchanged. By M5 eleven params files carried forty identical copies of them and the notes in four of those files already said so in words ('borrowed rather than re-tuned ... if this canvas ever needs its own, that is a finding'). M6 wants thirty canvases, so the borrowing is written down here instead of copied. params/<slug>.json is merged over this: it holds what is a fact about that canvas, and anything it overrides is the only tuning in it and is visible as tuning. The merged dict is what gets hashed, so no blob moved.
_scales: px at 120 px/cm. Canvas weave is ~9 px and brush-hair striation ~6 px; every smoothing scale here must sit above both or the tracer fits the cloth and the hairs.
_relief: BUILD.md M1. sigma_relief is the smoothing under the cross-profile: above the 9 px weave and the 6 px brush striation, well below a stroke's flank. The relief_* numbers are height method 2, which is geometry and never colour: a stroke stands as high as its own film, which goes with its width, plus the paint it was laid on, which the raster sums as it draws. They add -- multiplying them gives a big isolated loaded mark no height at all, because nothing crosses it, and on this canvas that is the sheaves. floor is because a stroke with no height is a decal. height_mm is the cap, applied everywhere and never exceeded, and it is the weakest number in this file: no scan in this set carries raking-light or photometric-stereo data, so it is set so the field's range matches the one published scan of Van Gogh-style impasto this build could check, which measured 1.1 mm peak to valley at 25 um. The width distribution here spans only 2.8x and cannot make a plausible relief alone; the stack spans six and does. order_lift_mm is the z-fight offset across the whole sequence, far below the cap and invisible. relief_sym_w only matters under --height 1.
_chroma: DESIGN 4.1 step 3: his strokes are very often one loaded colour beside another at the same value, which no luminance ridge can see. But taken as a plain union of the ridge maps it finds the same stroke three times -- measured on the gate tile, 99% of chroma traces ran within one stroke width of a luminance trace, for 2.3 points of coverage at 2.75x the strokes. veto_px is the radius around a luminance ridge inside which a chroma seed is refused: half a stroke width here, so chroma is seeded only where luminance is actually blind, which is what the design says. gain 0.01 puts a full-swing colour opposition at about the same number as a full-swing change in light. The energy floor stops coherence -- a ratio -- being asked where there is nothing to divide, so JPEG chroma noise in a flat passage cannot look like a stroke.
_seeds: spacing is about a quarter of a stroke width; below that the same stroke is seeded many times and dedup does all the work.
_trace: max_arc is BUILD's hard cap, 1024 px = 8.5 cm. Direction is blended with where the trace was already going, so the tensor's own jitter at a 6 px step does not read as curvature; max_turn then measures real bend. Total turn stops at 2.6 rad because past that no single quadratic can hold it and it should be a chain.
_attrs: width from the ridge out to the shadowed gap on either side, clipped to plausible paint: 1.2 mm to 1.6 cm. gap_frac is how much of that gap-to-gap distance is paint rather than the shadow between two marks. M0a had 0.72 and never looked at it at 1:1; drawing the fitted footprints on the scan shows 0.72 straddling two and three neighbouring marks, and the reconstruction at 1:1 is fat lozenges rather than ribbons. 0.50 puts the outlines on the marks. colour_band is deliberately narrow -- at 0.35 the median ate the neighbouring stroke and the whole palette collapsed toward its own mean, which is BUILD's 'mud'.
_merge: a trace whose centreline is mostly inside an already-claimed, similarly-directed footprint is the same stroke found twice.
_tiling: BUILD's numbers: 3072 px tiles stepping 2048, so 1024 px of overlap, which is the hard arc cap. Sizing an overlap against the mean arc rather than the cap is how you discover at station 8 that every long sky stroke has a seam in it.
_under: the ground seen between the strokes, extended beneath them. sigma is about twice a stroke width: broad enough that it cannot carry the picture (which the band-pass ratio checks), narrow enough to hold the tonal zones of the field.
_sigma_height: only --height 0 reads this: it is the wide neighbourhood of DESIGN 4.1 step 6, kept so that the estimate M1 replaced can still be reproduced and looked at.
